  Line or code reference: new paragraph in step 4, lines 35-45 (per the implement-plan log)
  Problem: The new auto-decision invokes `claude_fix_claim.py post … --kind hold` to post a hold claim after the phase PR opens, but `claude_fix_claim.py` (in `.claude/scripts/claude_fix_claim.py`, not modified by this PR) renders the "this PR reached the cap of 3 Claude hand-backs" sentence for every hold regardless of the actual reason. The new twin-first hold will therefore post a misleading "cap reached" comment on every protected-path phase PR.
  Why it fails at runtime: Every protected-path phase that triggers the new twin-first default will receive a hold claim comment claiming the cap was reached, when the actual reason is twin-sync (the master needs to copy the twins to `.claude/`) as `[claude-twin-sync]`. The plan's AD-8 and the lesson learned in `docs/implement-plan/issue-4948-protected-path-twin-first-default.md:51-56` explicitly capture this gap; the fix is deferred to the in-flight claude-fixer-unattended-convergence project (D15, phase 3: `--reason` on hold claims, which `/implement-plan-claude` passes for every hold it posts). Already observed on PR #5008 (comment 2026-09-29T04:03Z).
